questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Italy (Rome) because of the culture, the people, the university and the weather. And also getting a bit further away from Denmark than just Germany, Sweden or Norway...

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good experience. I had a lot of fun, I learned a bit and I met some nice people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. LUISS is very good at answering your questions - and they reply you within a day normally

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ESN (Erasmus Students Network) linked to LUISS arranged a welcoming week (mostly parties)... I don't know if this counts as assistance but it was fun. Also, I participated in the buddy programme and got linked with an Italian student from LUISS. We met a couple of times and he also invited me over for a party at his place. It got cancelled because of rain unfortunately.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I contacted LUISS Housing Service - Very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When studying political science you'll have all your classes at the Via Romania campus. You can try to find housing close to it but it's expensive (because the university is situated in the fancy Parioli neighborhood) and it's a bit far away from the center. I found a room in an apartment just 100 meters from the LUISS law campus (Via Pola) meaning that I lived around a 25 minutes walk from the Via Romania campus where I had my classes. What is very convenient is that LUISS has it's own shuttle service going forth and back from Via Pola and Via Romania. The shuttle service is dedicated to the students... So my recommendation might be to find something close to the Via Pola campus. Then you'll also live close to the Annibaliano metro station which is the easiest way to go to the city center. And you'll live close to Piazza Istria where a lot of LUISS students come to hang out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I found my apartment through LUISS Housing Service, I was living with four other exchange students from around the world. Although we had some different expectations about noise and cleaning in the kitchen, it all worked well and I got some really good friends out of it. I don't know if you'll live with other LUISS students no matter what if you find your apartment through the housing service but there is a good chance.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When applying for LUISS you'll only know the courses offered in the current academic year meaning that some courses can change. This is a bit frustrating as you have to get the "forhåndsgodkendelse" of your courses before leaving. When you get to LUISS and start taking your classes, you can change your courses in the first two weeks. This is a big bonus as you will then have time to find the right courses which can be approved by UCPH within the first two weeks of the semester. My advice would be to find courses now (as you are applying for the "forhåndsgodkendelse") that somehow fit the criteria from UCPH. Then, when you get to Rome you'll receive the list of courses offered on your semester 2-3 weeks before the semester starts and you'll have time to try out different courses and change your learning agreement so that it fits to the courses you are taking in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: LUISS - contact their international office and they will answer you quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful apart from one course that was not offered anyway. It wasn't a problem because it was an elective which could easily be substituted.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More presentations and debates... But you'll get used to it. See it as a challenge. Oral exams in front of the whole class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Institutions and Decision making, Comparative Politics, Comparative Public Policy in Europe, The Politics of Cultural Heritage in Europe, Russian History and Politics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Russian History and Politics because of professor Igor Pellichiari but is is now removed...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As written above, the ESN linked to LUISS organizes a welcoming week which I highly recommend. Here you can meet all the other international students, ask where they are from, what they are studying and repeat with the next.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trips around in Italy, sport clubs, football for the international students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN football league if you like football. Trips around in Italy were okay but can also easily be arranged by yourself with some friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Italy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, it's not that far from Denmark and people are quite open and welcoming (most of the time at least)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them...

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperitivo <3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The stuff I wrote above about housing, that Italy and Rome is a very exciting place to spent your semester, you don't have to pay for the bus (just be ready to activate your ticket). Remember to do trips out of Rome even though you are busy studying!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Participate in the welcoming week, relax, enjoy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friends I got (also from UCPH), to experience a new culture and country for 5 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my "forhåndsgodkendelse" in the beginning because none of the UCPH-offices answered me. I had to call three times to studievejledningen before something happened.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
